items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: Rob McConnell was our soloist, from the Boss Brass, and he had one arrangement on an old record of his that I loved... I says, 'Hey I want to do ‘Every Time We Say Goodbye.’'

ctx.x: Yeah. That was a great event. You guys did a good thing there with that orchestra.

We had a good time. And the guys in the band killed me though. Krissy sat in and she starts on the hi-hat [scats]. And the guys in the band would come in, and he says, “Why can’t she play with us?” — which was not really a compliment, but she did a nice job. I wanted her to play because the concert before, Rob McConnell was our soloist, from the Boss Brass, and he had one arrangement on an old record of his that I loved, “Every Time We Say Goodbye” — I says, “Hey I want to do ‘Every Time We Say Goodbye.’” He…
playing vibes on my next concert. Anyway, I’m waxing nostalgically here, but I’ve had a wonderful time in music.
